# swiftmap

> A Python mapping library that keeps Leaflet's ergonomics and replaces its vector
> drawing with WebGL pipelines — smooth at millions of points, not thousands.

swiftmap targets the gap between folium/ipyleaflet (good ergonomics, a ceiling around
tens of thousands of features, flat layer controls) and deck.gl (scales, but a different
mental model behind a thin Python layer). One rendering core serves four stacks:
Jupyter/anywidget notebooks, Shiny for Python, Streamlit, and React. Map state —
viewport, layer visibility, clicks, draws, the time slider — syncs bidirectionally
wherever there is a Python side to sync with. A finished map exports to a single static
HTML file that opens with no backend.

Everything runs offline: Leaflet, glify and Leaflet-Geoman ride inside the bundle that
ships in the wheel, so nothing is fetched when a map is viewed. On an air-gapped network
the wheel is the whole story.

## Install

- Python: `pip install swiftmap` (needs anywidget, numpy, xyzservices)
- JavaScript: `npm install swiftmap-core`
- Data sources: pandas, polars, geopandas and geostructures all work; none is a dependency.

## Links

- Docs and live demos: https://rkleisley.github.io/swiftmap/
- Source: https://github.com/Rkleisley/swiftmap
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/swiftmap/

## How it compares

- vs folium: same ease of use, roughly a hundredfold higher feature ceiling, plus
  hierarchical layer controls instead of a flat list.
- vs ipyleaflet: same widget model, WebGL rendering underneath, and it works outside
  notebooks (Shiny, Streamlit, React, static export).
- vs deck.gl: keeps the Leaflet mental model — `add_*` calls, no projection argument, no
  viewstate to manage — rather than a layer/viewstate API.
- vs kepler.gl: a library you call from code, not an application you configure.
- vs datashader: interactive vector features you can click, hover and toggle, rather than
  a rasterized image of your data.

## Naming

The npm package is `swiftmap-core`. The unscoped npm name `swiftmap` belongs to an
unrelated D3/TopoJSON library last published in 2018.
